newsitem.title: USA: Mobil says talks with "several" on U.S. link.
newsitem.headline: Mobil says talks with "several" on U.S. link.

text.p: Mobil Corp said Monday that it is in talks with "several" companies over a possible deal to link downstream assets.

"We are continually looking to improve marketing and refining in the U.S. We have had and continue to have discussions with several, and I emphasise the word 'several,' companies," said Christopher Springham, a spokesman for Mobil Corp.
"None has reached the stage where it is possible to reach any conclusions," he added.

Springham would not comment directly on a story in the business section of the Sunday Telegraph, a London newspaper, which quoted unnamed sources saying Mobil was "deep in talks" with Amoco Corp to merge their downstream interests in the U.S. and "overseas".
The newspaper article speculated that the deal would involve around $20 billion of assets.

U.S. oil analysts said last week that one of the rumors in the sector was that Mobil and BP America Inc, U.S. Unit of British Petroleum Co Plc, were in talks over the merger of their U.S. refining and marketing assets.
The two companies agreed about eighteen months ago to link their European downstream interests in the first major deal in the wave of global mergers which has swept the sector.
In the U.S., nine out of the top 25 refiners has been involved in a merger, acquisition or "alliance" in the past year and the sector is rife with rumors.
Last week, Marathon Oil Co and Ashland Inc agreed to link their U.S. downstream businesses in a 62/38 percent split.

Amoco has said several times that it is seeking a partner for its downstream assets and it is identified by analysts, together with such companies as Atlantic Richfield Co and Sun Co, as among those most keenly looking to hook up with a U.S. downstream partner.

An Amoco/Mobil U.S. downstream merger would link the number three and number five refiners with combined capacity to process nearly two million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil, according to the year-end worldwide refinery survey by the Oil & Gas Journal, a trade magazine.

The combined group would rival the proposed Shell Oil Co /Texaco Inc behemoth -- the two having last year agreed to merge their U.S. interests, including Texaco's joint venture with Saudi Aramco, Star Enterprises.

Amoco and Mobil both have large refineries in the south and mid-West. Mobil has medium-sized plants on the East and West coasts and in Louisiana. As well as its large Texas and Indiana refineries, Amoco has a smattering of plants scattered from Virginia to Utah.
Amoco officials were not immediately available for comment.
